instructions: Choose one response for each statement. Consider the past month unless the statement asks about earlier or longstanding patterns. Current or past concerns select areas for age-appropriate follow-up. Unsure and private responses need a clinician's review and are not counted as No. This original questionnaire does not diagnose a condition. Answer only from your observations or what the child has shared; do not guess about private experiences. A caregiver report does not replace the child's own confidential conversation with a clinician.

safety.text: In the past month, has the child said, shown or done anything suggesting suicide, not wanting to be alive or intentional self-harm?
In the past month, has the child expressed thoughts or urges to seriously harm someone else?
Right now, are you concerned that the child may act on harmful thoughts, be in danger or be unable to stay safe?

domains.title: Attention, learning and social communication
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child has difficulty with attention, organization or activity across everyday situations.
The child has longstanding difficulty learning reading, writing, mathematics or age-expected everyday skills.
Social communication, sensory differences or repetitive routines create difficulties for which the child may need support.

domains.title: Unusual perceptions and beliefs
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure. Consider experiences while fully awake; ordinary imaginative play and culturally shared beliefs alone do not indicate a disorder.

questions.text: While fully awake, the child reports hearing, seeing or sensing things that others do not seem to experience.
The child describes feeling watched, controlled or threatened in ways that concern me.
The child's thinking or speech sometimes becomes so hard to follow that communication or everyday activities are affected.

domains.title: Periods of unusually high energy
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child has had a distinct period of unusually elevated or irritable mood together with much more energy or activity than usual.
During a high-energy period, the child slept much less than usual without appearing tired.
During a high-energy period, unusually fast speech, thoughts or risky actions caused concern or consequences.

domains.title: Low mood and loss of interest
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child seems persistently sad, withdrawn, hopeless or unusually irritable.
The child has lost interest in friends, play or activities they usually enjoy.
Low mood, low energy or strong self-criticism interferes with the child's everyday life.

domains.title: Worry, fear and panic
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child shows worry or fear that is hard to settle.
The child has sudden episodes of intense fear or panic, sometimes with strong physical sensations.
Fear leads the child to avoid school, activities, other people or separation from caregivers.

domains.title: Intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child reports repeated unwanted thoughts or seems troubled by thoughts they cannot set aside.
The child feels driven to repeat actions or mental routines such as checking, washing, counting or asking for reassurance.
Difficulty discarding, appearance worries, skin picking or hair pulling causes distress or problems for the child.

domains.title: Reactions to trauma and major stress
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: Following a frightening or overwhelming experience, the child has unwanted memories, nightmares or repeated distress linked to it.
After a difficult experience, the child avoids reminders, seems emotionally cut off or stays unusually watchful or easily startled.
After major stress, change or loss, changes in the child's feelings or behavior interfere with everyday life.

domains.title: Detachment and gaps in awareness
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child describes feeling detached from their body or surroundings, or things seeming unreal.
The child has unexplained gaps in memory for important events beyond ordinary forgetting.
Changes in the child's awareness or sense of self cause confusion or distress.

domains.title: Physical symptoms and health-related distress
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure. Physical symptoms need appropriate medical attention; do not assume they are psychological.

questions.text: Physical symptoms cause substantial distress or interfere with the child's activities.
The child spends substantial time worrying about health or bodily sensations.
Repeated symptom checking, reassurance seeking or health-related avoidance is difficult for the child to manage.

domains.title: Eating and body-related concerns
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: Restricted eating or food avoidance may affect the child's growth, nutrition, health or daily life.
The child has out-of-control eating or tries to compensate through vomiting, medication misuse or excessive exercise.
Concerns about food or body size, or eating nonfood substances, cause problems for the child.

domains.title: Bladder and bowel concerns
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child has repeated wetting or urinary-control difficulties beyond what is expected for their developmental stage.
The child has repeated soiling or bowel-control difficulties beyond what is expected for their developmental stage.
Bladder or bowel difficulties cause the child distress, avoidance or disruption.

domains.title: Sleep and daytime alertness
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child has trouble falling asleep, staying asleep or waking at intended times.
The child is very sleepy during the day or not rested despite enough opportunity to sleep.
Breathing interruptions, unusual movements or behaviors during sleep, or a disrupted schedule affect the child.

domains.title: Body development and private well-being
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure. Do not record explicit details. This is a support screen, not an adult sexual-function assessment.

questions.text: The child has concerns about body development or private-body well-being that may benefit from a clinician's support.
The child has reported or shown pain or physical discomfort involving private parts of the body.
Body-related worries or discomfort interfere with the child's everyday life.

domains.title: Gender-related distress and support
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure. Gender identity or expression is not itself a symptom; these questions concern distress and requested support.

questions.text: The child has expressed distress about a mismatch between their experienced gender and aspects of their body or assigned sex.
Being treated as a gender that does not fit the child's experience causes distress.
The child may need support with gender-related stress, social pressure, bullying or discrimination.

domains.title: Anger and impulse control
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child has anger outbursts or aggressive actions that are hard to control.
Repeated impulsive actions harm the child, other people, property or important responsibilities.
Repeated serious conflicts, deception or rule violations create problems across home, school or other settings.

domains.title: Alcohol, drugs and gambling
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: I am concerned about the child's use of alcohol, nicotine, drugs or medications outside their intended use.
Substance use, cravings or possible withdrawal affects the child's health, safety, relationships or responsibilities.
Gambling or betting seems difficult for the child to control or has caused problems.

domains.title: Changes in thinking and previously learned skills
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure.

questions.text: The child's memory, attention or thinking has declined from their earlier level of functioning.
Changes in language, judgment, navigation or problem solving interfere with the child's everyday tasks.
The child shows confusion or has lost abilities they previously had.

domains.title: Developing coping and relationship patterns
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure. This does not assign a personality disorder; developmental context and clinical review are essential.

questions.text: Persistent patterns of conflict, mistrust or withdrawal disrupt the child's relationships across situations.
Ongoing difficulty managing emotions, impulses or sense of self creates problems beyond what seems expected for the child's development.
Repeated coping patterns interfere with relationships, school or home life and may need support.

domains.title: Body boundaries and sexual safety
domains.instructions: Consider the child's developmental stage and behavior across home, school, play and relationships. Use Not observed / do not know when unsure. Do not record explicit details. This does not assign a paraphilic diagnosis or infer abuse; discuss concerns directly with a qualified clinician.

questions.text: The child has shown or reported distress about sexual thoughts, experiences or boundary-related behavior that needs a private clinical discussion.
I am concerned about sexual behavior involving pressure, force, harm or another person unable or unwilling to agree.
The child may need support with body boundaries, sexual safety or controlling behavior that could harm someone.
